data.long_meaning: One who brings delight and pleasure. The name Aroosh carries the meaning “Delight, Pleasure” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Aroosh usually hope their child will grow to embody delight, pleasure and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies the presence of Allah's pleasure and happiness in one's life
data.etymology: Aroosh belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Delight, Pleasure.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aroosh total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Aroosh brings joy and happiness to its bearer and those around them. In various Islamic cultures, the name Aroosh is given to babies born into families that value joy, peace, and contentment. The name can also be given as a term of endearment to individuals who brighten up the room with their presence or demeanor.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Aroosh lies in its connection to the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) saying, "My Lord is gentle and loves gentleness." Aroosh represents a reminder of the gentle nature of Allah and the importance of cultivating a gentle and loving spirit. By bringing delight and pleasure to others, one can embody the spirit of Allah and create a beautiful and harmonious environment. The name Aroosh also reminds us of the hadith that states, "The believer's shade on the Day of Resurrection will be his character." Hence, being a source of joy and pleasure for others can be a characteristic that brings blessings and shade on the Day of Judgment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Delight, Pleasure" symbolizes One who brings delight and pleasure. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Aroosh serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of delight, pleasure.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah. Volume 8, page 310. The name Aroosh carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Aroosh ibn Rabia was a Sassanid Persian nobleman who converted to Islam before the Battle of Hunayn (633 AD). He was a prominent leader in the Muslim army and was granted the title of Amir Al-Mominin by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) for his bravery in the battle.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri's Ansab Al-Ashraf. Volume 1, page 101. The name Aroosh carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Aroosh ibn Jabalah Al-Himyari was the commander of the Himyarite army in Yemen during the Umayyad Caliphate. He rebelled against the Umayyads and allied himself with the Abbasid Caliphate. He was eventually defeated and killed in battle in 765 AD.
